summary: First-year university students map the friendships they have formed during their first semester. The study links the drinking of a student's friends to the student's own drinking (AUDIT-C) and wellbeing (WHO-5).

stages.title: introduction title
stages.text: introduction text: what taking part involves
stages.draft: This study asks about the friends you have made since starting university, about drinking alcohol, and about how you have been feeling. It takes about 20 minutes. Your answers are confidential, and you can stop at any time.

stages.purpose: Welcome the participant and explain the study.
stages.title: screen title
stages.draft: Thank you for taking part. We will ask about the people you have got to know since starting university, about drinking, and about how you have been feeling.

stages.purpose: Elicit friends and the people the participant spends time with at university.
stages.title: introduction screen title; draft: "Naming people"
stages.text: introduction screen text: what the next screen asks the participant to do, and how
stages.draft: On the next screen you will be asked a question. Tap the add button, then type the name of each person who comes to mind and press Enter. Move on when you have added everyone.

stages.purpose: Elicit friends and the people the participant spends time with at university.
stages.title: none: return ""

stages.purpose: When and where each tie formed.
stages.title: introduction screen title; draft: "About the people you named"
stages.text: introduction screen text: what the next screen asks the participant to do, and how
stages.draft: Next, you will answer a few questions about each of the people you named, one at a time.

stages.purpose: When and where each tie formed.
stages.title: none: return ""

stages.purpose: Closeness, how they met, and perceived heavy drinking for everyone named.

stages.draft: On the next screen you will see the people you named and a set of boxes. Drag each person into the box that describes them best.

stages.purpose: Closeness, how they met, and perceived heavy drinking for everyone named.
stages.title: none: return ""

stages.purpose: Arrange the network, record who knows whom, and mark drinking companions.
stages.title: introduction screen title; draft: "Your network map"
stages.text: introduction screen text: what the next screen asks the participant to do, and how
stages.draft:
On the next screen you will see the people you named on a map, with you at the centre.

Drag each of the people onto the circles. The closer to the centre you place someone, the closer they are to you.

To connect two of the people, tap one and then the other. Do the same again to remove a connection.

Tap each person the question describes. Tap them again to undo.

stages.purpose: Arrange the network, record who knows whom, and mark drinking companions.
stages.title: none: return ""

stages.purpose: How often the participant drinks with each drinking companion.

stages.purpose: Thank the participant and list support resources.
stages.title: screen title
stages.draft: Thank you for taking part. If anything in this interview has worried you, your university student support or wellbeing service can help, and your doctor can give confidential advice about drinking.

prompts.draft: Since **starting university this semester**, who have you **become friends with**?
Who do you **spend most of your free time with** at university?
Who would you **turn to for support** if something was worrying you?
Drag each person into the box that best describes **how close you feel** to them.
How did you **first meet** each person?
As far as you know, does each person often **drink heavily** (five or more drinks on one occasion)?
Place the people you are **closest to** nearest the centre.
Draw a line between any two people who **know each other**.
Tap everyone you **usually drink alcohol with**.
How often do you **drink alcohol together** with each person?

questions.draft: Do you agree to take part in this study?
How do you describe your gender?
Do you live in university accommodation (halls)?
Is this person also a first-year student?
When did you first meet this person?
